candidate.statement: CDKN2A-loss cell lines (frequently co-deleted with MTAP at 9p21) exhibit enhanced synthetic lethal dependency on PRMT5 knockout compared to CDKN2A-intact cell lines.
queries: CDKN2A MTAP deletion PRMT5 dependency CRISPR DepMap
MTAP CDKN2A loss PRMT5 essentiality cancer cell lines

review.rationale: The candidate proposes that CDKN2A loss (frequently co-deleted with MTAP at 9p21) confers enhanced synthetic lethal dependency on PRMT5 knockout compared to intact cell lines. MED:40694540 specifically confirms that CDKN2A/MTAP codeletion occurs frequently in NSCLC and solid tumors, and establishes PRMT5 as a synthetic-lethal dependency in MTAP-null / CDKN2A-deleted tumors. MED:39282709 also corroborates that MTAP deletion confers PRMT5 dependency identified via functional genomic screens across multiple lineages.

candidate.statement: KEAP1-mutant/deficient NSCLC cell lines display increased dependency on NFE2L2 (NRF2) knockout compared to KEAP1-wildtype lines due to oncogene addiction to constitutive NRF2 antioxidant signaling.
queries: KEAP1 mutant NFE2L2 essentiality non-small cell lung cancer

review.rationale: MED:40676628 empirically demonstrates that lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) cell lines with active NRF2/KEAP1 mutations depend on NRF2 for survival/viability, whereas cells with normal NRF2 do not require NRF2 under non-stress conditions, and NRF2 depletion causes cell death specifically in active-NRF2/KEAP1-deficient models. MED:42255480, MED:41417010, and MED:36632216 further substantiate the oncogene addiction and selective dependency on NFE2L2/NRF2 in KEAP1-mutant/deficient NSCLC.

candidate.statement: MSI-high cancer cell lines demonstrate profound synthetic lethal dependency on the WRN helicase compared to microsatellite-stable cell lines.

review.rationale: MED:30971823 analyzed large-scale CRISPR-Cas9 knockout and RNA interference screens across cancer cell line models and demonstrated that WRN is selectively essential in microsatellite instability (MSI) models while being dispensable in microsatellite-stable models. This is further corroborated by multiple sources confirming WRN helicase dependency as a synthetic lethal vulnerability in MSI cancer models.

candidate.statement: In the subgroup defined by high research_signature_a and low research_signature_b, PTEN loss associates with altered dependency on STAT3 in NSCLC cell lines.
queries: PTEN loss STAT3 dependency lung cancer CRISPR
PTEN deletion STAT3 essentiality NSCLC DepMap

review.rationale: None of the provided abstracts demonstrate an established association between PTEN loss and STAT3 CRISPR knockout dependency specifically in NSCLC cell lines or within the specified research signature subgroup. While MED:41287778 describes hypersensitivity to STAT3 inhibition in PTEN-deficient colorectal cancer, this does not establish an expected CRISPR dependency in NSCLC. Therefore, the candidate appropriately represents a neutral hypothesis without an established directional expectation in this lineage and subgroup.

candidate.statement: Within NSCLC cell lines stratified by elevated research_signature_b and research_signature_c, CDKN2A loss is associated with differential dependency on MDM2.
queries: CDKN2A loss MDM2 dependency lung cancer DepMap
p16 CDKN2A MDM2 CRISPR dependency NSCLC

review.rationale: The candidate is proposed as a neutral discovery assessing whether CDKN2A loss is associated with differential MDM2 dependency in NSCLC cell lines stratified by novel research signatures. None of the retrieved literature establishes an empirical directional association for this specific combination of genomic alteration, target dependency, lineage, and subgroup. Thus, consistent with guidelines for neutral candidates lacking established prior directional expectations, the proposal is classified as neutral.
